author: D

components.title: Part A business day date
components.what: Count 88 business days from 2026-03-19 skipping weekends and the six listed holidays to find the resulting date.

components.title: Part B inclusion-exclusion count
components.what: Count integers 1 to 8000 divisible by 3, 5, or 7 but not 13 using inclusion-exclusion and floor division.

components.title: Part C CRT solution
components.what: Solve the system n≡8 mod 19, n≡0 mod 17, n≡10 mod 23 using the Chinese remainder theorem.

log.author: B
log.draft:
Part A: Counting weekdays after 2026-03-19 and excluding the listed holidays:

8 + 19 + 20 + 20 + 21 = 88, reaching 2026-07-29. The supplied Python `datetime` check also gives 2026-07-29.

Part B: Inclusion-exclusion gives the count divisible by at least one of 3, 5, or 7:

2666 + 1600 + 1142 - 533 - 380 - 228 + 76 = 4343.

Those also divisible by 13 total:

205 + 123 + 87 - 41 - 29 - 17 + 5 = 333.

Thus, 4343 - 333 = 4010.

Part C: Set \(n=17k\). Solving \(17k\equiv8\pmod{19}\) gives \(k\equiv15\pmod{19}\), so \(n=323m+255\). Then \(n\equiv10\pmod{23}\) gives \(m\equiv8\pmod{23}\), hence \(n=7429t+2839\). The smallest positive solution is 2839, verified by remainders 8, 0, and 10 modulo 19, 17, and 23.

FINAL: 2026-07-29; 4010; 2839

challenges.problem: The day counts per month and the final date are miscalculated. 2026-03-19 is a Thursday. March has 8 remaining business days (March 20, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 30, 31). April 2026 has 22 weekdays minus 3 listed holidays (Apr 3, 9, 24) = 19 days. May 2026 has 21 weekdays minus 1 holiday (May 13) = 20 days. June 2026 has 22 weekdays minus 2 holidays (Jun 18, 29) = 20 days. Subtotal through end of June is 8 + 19 + 20 + 20 = 67 days. To reach 88 business days, we need 88 - 67 = 21 business days in July. July 2026 has no listed holidays. The 21st weekday of July 2026 is Wednesday, 2026-07-29 (July 1 is Wednesday; 4 full weeks of 5 days = 20 days ending Tuesday July 28; the 21st day is July 29). While the final date 2026-07-29 happens to be correct, the draft's internal arithmetic claimed 21 days reaches July 29 without explicitly defining July's calendar alignment. More critically, verify if 2026-03-19 itself is excluded properly: 8 business days in March is correct (20th to 31st), but panel should verify whether any holidays fall on weekends: 2026-04-03 (Fri), 2026-04-09 (Thu), 2026-04-24 (Fri), 2026-05-13 (Wed), 2026-06-18 (Thu), 2026-06-29 (Mon). All 6 are weekdays.

Check modular conditions: 2839 % 17 = 0 (2839 = 17 * 167); 2839 % 19 = 19 * 149 + 8 = 2839 (remainder 8); 2839 % 23 = 23 * 123 + 10 = 2839 (remainder 10). Modulo is 17 * 19 * 23 = 7429. Since 2839 < 7429 and positive, it is strictly the minimal positive integer.

The date is asserted without showing the weekday/holiday calendar walk-through, and the arithmetic line '8 + 19 + 20 + 20 + 21 = 88' does not identify which months those partial counts correspond to or verify that the six listed holidays were skipped.

The inclusion-exclusion subtotals for multiples of 13 are not derived from explicit floor divisions, and the final subtraction assumes all multiples of 13 among the union were counted exactly once, but no list of the seven floor terms for the 13-filtered set is shown.
The CRT derivation is unsupported: it states k≡15 mod 19 and m≡8 mod 23 without showing the modular arithmetic, and the final solution is not checked against all three congruences explicitly.

log.answer:
Part A: 2026-03-19 is Thursday. Remaining March business days: 8 (Mar 20, 23–27, 30–31). April: 22 weekdays − 3 holidays (Apr 3, 9, 24) = 19. May: 21 weekdays − 1 holiday (May 13) = 20. June: 22 weekdays − 2 holidays (Jun 18, 29) = 20. Through June: 67, so need 21 in July. July 1, 2026 is Wednesday; the 21st July weekday is July 29.

Part B: Count divisible by 3,5,7:
⌊8000/3⌋=2666, ⌊8000/5⌋=1600, ⌊8000/7⌋=1142, subtract ⌊8000/15⌋=533, ⌊8000/21⌋=380, ⌊8000/35⌋=228, add ⌊8000/105⌋=76: total 4343.
Divisible also by 13:
⌊8000/39⌋=205, ⌊8000/65⌋=123, ⌊8000/91⌋=87, subtract ⌊8000/195⌋=41, ⌊8000/273⌋=29, ⌊8000/455⌋=17, add ⌊8000/1365⌋=5: total 333.
Answer 4343−333=4010.

Part C: Let n=17k. 17k≡8 mod19. 17^{-1}≡9 mod19, so k≡72≡15 mod19, hence n=323m+255. Mod23: 323≡1, 255≡2, so m+2≡10, m≡8. Thus n=323·8+255=2839. Check: 2839 mod19=8, mod17=0, mod23=10.

FINAL: 2026-07-29; 4010; 2839

asked: Part A: the record never states the weekday anchor used to establish that 2026-03-19 is a Thursday and that 2026-07-01 is a Wednesday. What independent source or day-of-week computation (e.g. Doomsday/Zeller for 2026) confirms both anchors, and does the count treat the start date 2026-03-19 as excluded (day 0) rather than counted?

Part A: does July 2026 contain exactly 23 weekdays, and does the 21st weekday of July 2026 land on 2026-07-29 given July 1 is a Wednesday? Please list the July weekday sequence positions 20, 21, 22 (dates) so the off-by-one at the boundary is settled.

Part B: the phrase 'divisible by at least one of 3, 5, or 7 but not divisible by 13' is interpreted as |union(3,5,7)| minus |union(3,5,7) and 13|. Is there any reading under which the 13-exclusion should apply only to the multiples counted once, and can you confirm the subtracted set 333 is exactly the count of n<=8000 divisible by 13 and by at least one of 3,5,7 (i.e. multiples of 39, 65, or 91 under inclusion-exclusion)?
replies: No source was stated in the submitted answer. Independent Doomsday computation: 2026 has doomsday Saturday (2000 doomsday Tuesday + 26 + floor(26/4) = Tuesday + 32 ≡ Saturday). Since 3/14 is a doomsday, 2026-03-19 is Thursday; since 7/11 is a doomsday, 2026-07-01 is Wednesday. The count treats 2026-03-19 as excluded/day 0: the first counted day is Friday 2026-03-20, and the listed 8 remaining March business days are Mar 20, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 30, 31.

Yes. July 2026 has 31 days starting Wednesday, so it has 23 weekdays (4 full weeks = 20 weekdays plus Wed, Thu, Fri). With July 1 as position 1, the July weekday positions are: 20 = 2026-07-28 (Tue), 21 = 2026-07-29 (Wed), 22 = 2026-07-30 (Thu). Thus the 21st weekday is 2026-07-29.

The standard reading is exactly |union(3,5,7)| minus |union(3,5,7) ∩ multiples of 13|. There is no plausible reading where the 13-exclusion applies only to a subset of the counted multiples; 'but not divisible by 13' filters every number in the union. The subtracted set is exactly multiples of 39, 65, or 91, counted by inclusion-exclusion: 205 + 123 + 87 − 41 − 29 − 17 + 5 = 333. Therefore 4343 − 333 = 4010.

asked: Part A: the record subtracts all six holidays as if each falls on a Monday-Friday. Using the same 2026 doomsday anchor, what weekday is each of 2026-04-03, 2026-04-09, 2026-04-24, 2026-05-13, 2026-06-18, 2026-06-29, and is any of them a Saturday or Sunday (which would make its subtraction an error)?

Part A: what are the independently verified raw weekday counts for April 2026 (claimed 22), May 2026 (claimed 21), and June 2026 (claimed 22), including the weekday of the 1st and last day of each month, so the running total of 67 through June can be checked?

Part B: can you confirm each floor value used in the union count, specifically floor(8000/3)=2666, floor(8000/5)=1600, floor(8000/7)=1142, floor(8000/15)=533, floor(8000/21)=380, floor(8000/35)=228, floor(8000/105)=76, and that these sum under inclusion-exclusion to 4343?
replies:
4. Using 2026 doomsday Saturday (2026-01-01 is Thursday, so 2026-01-03 is Saturday; 4/4, 6/6, 7/11, etc. are Saturday): 2026-04-03 is Friday, 2026-04-09 is Thursday, 2026-04-24 is Friday, 2026-05-13 is Wednesday, 2026-06-18 is Thursday, 2026-06-29 is Monday. None is a Saturday or Sunday, so subtracting all six holidays is not an error.
5. April 2026: Apr 1 = Wednesday, Apr 30 = Thursday; 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 extra weekdays (Wed, Thu), so 22 weekdays. May 2026: May 1 = Friday, May 31 = Sunday; 31 days = 4 weeks + 3 extra days (Fri, Sat, Sun), giving 1 extra weekday, so 21 weekdays. June 2026: Jun 1 = Monday, Jun 30 = Tuesday; 30 days = 4 weeks + 2 extra weekdays (Mon, Tue), so 22 weekdays. Running total through June: 8 + (22-3) + (21-1) + (22-2) = 8+19+20+20 = 67, as claimed.
6. floor(8000/3)=2666 (3*2666=7998, 3*2667=8001); floor(8000/5)=1600; floor(8000/7)=1142 (7*1142=7994, 7*1143=8001); floor(8000/15)=533 (15*533=7995); floor(8000/21)=380 (21*380=7980, 21*381=8001); floor(8000/35)=228 (35*228=7980); floor(8000/105)=76 (105*76=7980). Inclusion-exclusion sum: 2666+1600+1142-533-380-228+76 = 4343. All confirmed.
